question: The resistivity of a metallic conductor increases when its temperature is raised. Explain why this happens. Give reason.

options.A: With rise in temperature, free electrons stop colliding with lattice ions, so resistivity decreases.
options.B: With rise in temperature, the number of free electrons becomes zero, so resistivity increases.
options.C: With rise in temperature, lattice-ion vibrations increase, causing more frequent electron collisions and a smaller relaxation time; hence resistivity increases.
options.D: With rise in temperature, the length of a metal wire always decreases, so resistivity increases.
